subject.title: [Feature]: only accept signed messages to prevent prompt injection [improvement] [hardening]

question: Should owner-key signed inbound-message verification be a core/SDK security capability, a channel/hook plugin pattern, or rejected as overlapping existing pairing and allowlists?
rationale: The request changes where OpenClaw draws the inbound trust boundary and would require choices about key registration, per-channel policy, logs, and whether #81061 is the right extension point.

options.title: Plugin or hook verification first
options.body: Keep core lean by documenting or building a ClawHub/plugin pattern for email or channel-specific signature checks, then extend SDK only for missing pre-routing suppression.

options.title: Define generic SDK capability
options.body: Design a typed pre-agent signature-verification capability with config, key storage, audit logging, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Reject universal signatures
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers decide pairing, allowlists, platform auth, and tool policy are the intended security model for this threat.

recommendation.title: Plugin or hook verification first
recommendation.body: Keep core lean by documenting or building a ClawHub/plugin pattern for email or channel-specific signature checks, then extend SDK only for missing pre-routing suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent security-doc and plugin-boundary history plus official project decision ownership make this the best available product/security routing owner.
